abstract: We study the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation and establish global uniqueness for weak solutions. The key idea comes from the weak uniqueness in the uniform-in-time high-frequency threshold (UTHT) class introduced in [12,14]. We derive a new energy defect threshold (EDT) criterion from the UTHT criterion. Along the strong solution flow, energy conservation propagates the EDT condition for weak solutions and, combined with the global well-posedness theory for strong solutions, yields global weak uniqueness. As an application, we prove unconditional uniqueness for the quintic defocusing energy-critical Gross-Pitaevskii hierarchy.
hook: Weak solutions of the defocusing energy-critical Schrodinger equation are globally unique.
summary: The authors prove that weak solutions of this nonlinear wave equation cannot branch, using a new energy defect threshold condition that energy conservation carries along the strong solution flow. They apply it to show unconditional uniqueness for the quintic Gross-Pitaevskii hierarchy, a model of many interacting bosons. The result is mathematical and applies to the defocusing energy-critical case only.
title: Uniqueness of global weak solutions for the defocusing energy-critical NLS
